messages:
maya: Heads up — onboarding Sidera17b (sparse-int4 variant) is hitting CUDA OOMs in canary. Seen on two nodes in eu-west-1.

raj: Yep saw that. Repro steps?

maya: curl to our inference endpoint with a stress prompt (long conv -> 4k tokens). cmd: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"sidera-17b-sparse-int4-v1","prompt":"<long chat>","max_new_tokens":512,"batch_size":2}'`

linus: paste of the pod logs: ```
E tensorflow: CUDA OOM when allocating 512MB (requested by sparse_matmul_kernel)
E runtime: fragmentation: free fragments: 48 MB avg, largest free: 16 MB, total free: 384 MB
E inference: failed step prefetch + kv_alloc -> OOM
```

anya: interesting — fragmentation numbers look like sparse kernels cause many small allocations. Could be our sparse matmul using many temporary buffers.

raj: quick mitigation options: 1) disable sparse kernel path for that model (fall back to dense GEMM), 2) reduce max_new_tokens default to 256 for canary, 3) enforce batch_concurrency=1 for the node pool, 4) enable kv_trim on generate end.

maya: tried (2) and (3) quickly — reduced incidents but still one OOM after a long session. Disabling sparse kernel removed the OOM on the same trace.

linus: concrete config diff I pushed to the canary: ```yaml
model_overrides:
  sidera-17b-sparse-int4-v1:
    runtime.flags:
      use_sparse_kernels: false
    defaults:
      max_new_tokens: 256
      batch_concurrency: 1
    kv_trim_on_response: true
```

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 3/5 hosts updated for sidera-17b-sparse-int4-v1 (use_sparse_kernels=false) :rocket:

anya: long-term we should: 1) add a microbench for sparse kernel temp allocs, 2) upstream a patch to reuse temp buffers in sparse_matmul, 3) add a slot compactor heuristic to coalesce small free blocks sooner.

raj: also add evals: compare quality (LLM bench) between sparse off (dense GEMM int4) vs sparse-on. We must ensure disabling sparse kernel doesn't regress perplexity or generation metrics.

maya: did a quick QA run: BLEU-like and safety checks looked fine for small prompts but we need full convo evals. Adding to the onboarding checklist: `quant-sparse-kernel-smoke` test + mem-frag monitor.

linus: temporary alert rule suggestion: trigger when fragmentation largest_free < 2x average_request_chunk and OOM rate > 0.5% over 5m, then auto-fall back to dense kernel for that model and notify #eng-ml.

anya: one more note — the OOM stack points at our prefetch path allocating KV slices before kernel selection. Propose moving kernel selection earlier so prefetch uses the right alloc pattern.

maya: filing a follow-up RFC and a canary rollback plan. For now canary continues with sparse disabled.

raj: tasks:
- linus: microbench for sparse tmp buffers (ETA 2d)
- anya: slot compactor heuristic draft (ETA 3d)
- maya: full eval compare dense vs sparse (ETA 2d)
- infra: add frag-based alert + auto-fallback (ETA 1d)

maya: thx all — will post updates here. :eyes:
